units.eff_n: fraction 0-1 (maximum retention efficiency of this cover)
units.crit_len_n: m (distance over which retention reaches ~half its maximum)
units.proportion_subsurface_n: fraction 0-1 of the N load that travels subsurface (P has no subsurface term in InVEST NDR)

definition: Per-land-cover nutrient export loads (a 'nutrient runoff proxy'-weighted source term) and the vegetation's capacity to retain nutrients moving through it. InVEST NDR distributes each pixel's load downslope and removes a fraction as flow passes through retentive cover, governed by eff and crit_len.

how_to_estimate.summary: Loads: from an export-coefficient dataset for your region (best), or from fertiliser application rates (Ludemann 2022) times an export fraction, or adopt a published InVEST NDR parameter set from a comparable biome. Efficiencies and critical lengths: adopt from a published InVEST NDR study - very few are measured directly; the InVEST User Guide and Redhead et al. (2018) / Raji et al. (2020) are the common starting points.

how_to_choose: Loads are climate- and agronomy-specific - match region and cropping intensity, not just the word 'cropland'. eff and crit_len are more transferable but still depend on vegetation structure: dense woody buffers retain more over shorter distances (high eff, short-to-moderate crit_len); grass strips need more length. Keep eff_p <= ~0.8 and crit_len_p short (10-30 m) - P moves mostly with sediment and drops out fast. proportion_subsurface_n is high (0.4-0.5) under woody/perennial cover (much N goes to groundwater) and low (0.2-0.3) under settlements/cropland with overland dominance. Always tag the source_key.
